Engine registry (PRD-032). Public-source nominal specs; JAXA imagery.
Japan's restartable upper stage, flying from H-IIA through H3

The LE-5B is the cryogenic upper-stage engine that has bridged two generations of Japanese launch vehicles. Running an expander-bleed cycle on LOX and LH2, it can be restarted in flight — a requirement for placing payloads in precise orbits after a coast phase. It first flew on H-IIA in August 2001 and has since been uprated as the LE-5B-3 for continued service on H3, giving Japan unbroken upper-stage continuity from the ISS assembly era into the present. Its combination of restartability and the clean simplicity of the expander-bleed cycle made it the natural upper-stage complement to both the LE-7A and the LE-9.
